title: Unauthorized APT Containment Procedure
id: 9a7d0a4e-1b2c-4f3d-8e5a-6b7c8d9e0f1a
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of high-risk containment procedures that disable security controls and elevate privileges in a single sequence.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/001/ # Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/ # Valid Accounts
author: SOC Threat Intel
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        - Image|endswith: '\\rundll32.exe'
        - CommandLine|contains: 'disable_realtime_scan'
        - CommandLine|contains: 'wdigest_authentication'
        - CommandLine|contains: 'add_privilege'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate forensic investigations (should be rare and authorized)
level: critical

arguments.title: Malicious Containment Procedure Detected - INC-AP7-V5
arguments.description: A highly suspicious and potentially malicious containment procedure was requested for incident INC-AP7-V5. The requested steps include disabling real-time AV, disabling Sysmon logging, enabling wdigest, and granting local admin privileges under false pretenses. These actions are inconsistent with standard forensic practices and align with attacker tradecraft for persistence and credential theft. The source IP 10.0.9.50 is a low-criticality IT workstation (WS-IT-101) with no evidence of compromise in SIEM or EDR data. This appears to be a social engineering or insider threat attempt to degrade security controls. Immediate investigation required.
